title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, and any person who by their role or otherwise becomes aware of Inside Information by having access to confidential material such as board papers or periodic disclosure materials. Extends to their spouse or children under 18, a trust of which they or family are trustee or beneficiary, and a company they or their family control.

tiers.name: Employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
tiers.description: Employees, consultants and contractors who are not Designated Persons; may deal at any time absent Inside Information, with no black-out periods or general approval requirement, though clause 6.2 gates their use of Derivatives regardless of tier.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products or hedging arrangement or other arrangement which operates to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's quarterly results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's half-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's half-year results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's full-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's full-year results

windows.start_anchor: 21 calendar days before the Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: date of the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairperson, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may determine any other period to be a Black-out Period from time to time; confidentiality of such a determination is not addressed.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on using Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments including performance share rights.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested Company Securities still subject to a disposal restriction such as a Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unrestricted positions are permitted subject to prior approval of the Chairperson (or the Board where the Chairperson is dealing) and compliance with the law and the rest of the Policy. Unlike the general clearance regime under clause 5 (which only binds Designated Persons), this derivatives gate applies regardless of tier.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) and subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy, be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: 'Hedging arrangement' is expressly named within the Derivatives definition, and Derivatives are banned outright over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products or hedging arrangement or other arrangement which operates to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: A hedging arrangement over vested unrestricted securities is a Derivative, permitted with prior Chairperson (or Board) approval, applicable regardless of tier.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) ... be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward sale is a 'forward contract' within the Derivatives definition and an agreement to dispose of securities within Dealing, so it is caught by the ban on Derivatives over unvested instruments.
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation of vested unrestricted shares is a Derivative/Dealing permitted subject to prior Chairperson (or Board) approval.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of, securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named and is not listed within the Dealing or Derivatives definitions.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named but fall within the section 761D derivatives concept incorporated into the Derivatives definition, so a CFD over unvested instruments is banned.
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: A CFD over vested unrestricted shares is a Derivative permitted with prior Chairperson (or Board) approval.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) ... be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Designated Persons may not enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities, nor use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement, regardless of vesting state.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.tier: Employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
rules.detail: Clause 6.3 is expressly addressed to Designated Persons only; it is silent as to other employees, consultants or contractors.
Using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement is expressly banned; a charge or lien unconnected to a funding arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement

rules.detail: The ban extends beyond margin loans strictly so-called to any 'similar funding arrangement' secured on Company Securities, for Designated Persons only, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or ... use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or intention-based short-term dealing restriction is imposed; clause 6.1 only governs the continuation of pending buy/sell orders once a Black-out Period commences.

clearance.approver: Chairperson or the Board (Board approves if the Chairperson is the one dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Designated Person (other than the Chairperson) wishing to Deal in Company Securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairperson or the Board before doing so. ... any Designated Person who Deals in Company Securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within five business days of the Dealing occurring.

clearance.tier: Employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
clearance.evidence: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information and provided such Dealing otherwise complies with applicable laws.

exceptions.evidence: the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities

the Designated Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement for them to do so.

exercise (but not Deal with the securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person.
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class.

participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board.

exemption_authority: The Chairperson (Approval Officer) may grant Disposal Consent for sale/transfer only, in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court order/enforceable undertaking), on terms and conditions considered reasonable by the Approval Officer, with the Board notified of any consent granted; not stated to be confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly banned for Designated Persons with no vesting carve-out and no approval or exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) and subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy, be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the general Dealing approval regime (limited to Designated Persons), this gate applies to any employee, consultant or contractor who wants to use a Derivative, meaning even non-Designated staff would need Chairperson sign-off for the option legs of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging arrangement named in Derivatives definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: any other transaction in financial products or hedging arrangement or other arrangement which operates to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging is expressly captured (not merely implied) within Derivatives, so the collar's put and call legs are unambiguously 'Derivatives' subject to the unvested ban and the Chairperson/Board approval gate on vested unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chairperson (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Disposal Consent covers sale/transfer only, initiating a new collar (acquiring a put, writing a call, or granting security) cannot be done during a Black-out Period even under hardship.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their spouse or any of their children (including step children) under the age of 18 years; a trust which they, any members of their family, or family controlled company are a trustee or beneficiary; and a company which they or their family control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, minor child's holding, family trust or controlled company does not escape the Designated Person's approval requirement or the secured financing ban.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a Designated Person (which will typically include any director or KMP the bank would approach) because clause 6.3 expressly bans Designated Persons from using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or 'similar funding arrangement', with no vesting carve-out, approval route or exemption authority. The unfunded derivative legs are separately gated: Derivatives (expressly including hedging arrangements, options, forwards, caps and collars) are banned outright over unvested performance rights and over vested shares still subject to a disposal restriction such as a Holding Lock, but are permitted over vested, unrestricted shares subject to prior approval of the Chairperson (or the Board where the Chairperson is dealing) - a gate that, unusually, applies to every tier, not just Designated Persons - plus notification to the Company Secretary within five business days for Designated Persons. Execution must occur outside the quarterly, half-year and full-year results black-outs and the 21-day AGM black-out (and any Chairperson-determined ad hoc black-out) and while the person holds no Inside Information; the only exceptional-circumstances relief (hardship or court order) is for disposal/transfer only and cannot support acquiring a put, writing a call, or granting security. Overall, the derivative legs of a collar could in principle be cleared for vested, unlocked shares, but the secured loan leg is prohibited outright for the tier the bank is targeting.
